Package io.github.janglada.orkit.routing

package io.github.janglada.orkit.routing
Vehicle routing solver.

Offers a fluent DSL for modeling vehicle routing problems (VRP): one or more depots, vehicles with capacities, stops with demands and time windows, pluggable distance sources, first-solution heuristics and local-search metaheuristics.

Multiple depots. depot(id, lat, lon) is accumulative — call it once per depot; the first registered depot is the default. Assign a vehicle to a depot with VehicleConfig.startsAt(String) / VehicleConfig.endsAt(String) (a vehicle may start and end at different depots). A vehicle with no assignment uses the default depot for both ends. Depot ids are resolved at solve time; an unknown id raises ModelException. Each solved Route reports its start depot via Route.depotId().

Capacities, time and cost. Vehicles and stops may declare several named capacity dimensions; stops may have hard windows and soft deadlines; vehicles may have availability windows, route-duration caps, driver breaks, and per-meter and per-minute costs used by Goals.totalCost(). The solver reports every accepted solution through RoutingSolver.onSolution(java.util.function.Consumer<io.github.janglada.orkit.routing.RoutingPlan>) and can start from an earlier plan through RoutingSolver.warmStart.

Limitation: no time-dependent travel. The native OR-Tools RoutingModel transit callback is a pure function of (fromNode, toNode) (optionally vehicle) and cannot read the arrival-time variable, so travel time cannot vary by time of day. travelSpeedKmh is therefore a single global scalar, not a time-banded speed profile. Static time windows and per-vehicle depots are fully supported; true time-dependent travel would require a CP-SAT routing solver and is not yet implemented.

Entry point: Optimize.vehicleRouting().
